summary: The 2002 Tokyo Mew Mew anime stretches a 27-chapter manga over 52 episodes, so roughly 40% of the run is anime-original and the canon spine is NOT adapted in manga order. Episodes 1-13 are a clean linear adaptation of chapters 1-10 (the only stretch where per-episode chapter data actually exists on the wiki: tokyomewmew.fandom.com fills the episode-infobox 'chapter' field for eps 1-4 and the reverse 'anime' field on chapter pages 1-5, then stops - every later episode page carries a literal '...' placeholder). From ep 17 on the adaptation shuffles: the Blue Knight debut (ch 16) and his duel with Quiche (ch 17) are pulled FORWARD to eps 17-18, then eps 25-28 go BACK to fill in ch 14-15 (Tokyo Tower waiburn), ch 16 (the rain confession) and ch 12-13 (Ichigo trapped as a cat); ep 36 takes ch 20-21 before ep 38 covers ch 19 and ep 40 covers ch 18. The endgame is linear and unambiguous again: ep 49 = ch 24, ep 50 = ch 25, ep 51 = ch 26, ep 52 = ch 27 (the manga's final chapter), with the mock wedding swapped for an a la Mode sequel hook. Chapter 11 (TokyoPop 'Cruise Control', Pie attacking a cruise ship) has no anime counterpart at all. Anchors below are deliberately kept MONOTONIC on furthest-first-time coverage; the out-of-order backfill episodes are recorded as annotations rather than forced into anchors, and the chapter-space conflict (AniList 33 / MangaDex 32 / en.wp prose 29 / chapter-list-and-our-stored-volume-boundaries 27) is flagged.

anchors.note: Earthquake at the endangered-species exhibit through Ichigo's first transformation and the Ryou/Keiichiro reveal - fandom episode infobox states 'Ch. 1' and the Chapter 1 page states 'Ep. 1'.
Mint recruited after her dog is infected - fandom episode infobox 'Ch. 2', Chapter 2 page reverse-maps to 'Ep. 2'.

Lettuce as the pool 'ghost' (ch 3) plus the tail of ch 4 - the episode ends on Quiche stealing Ichigo's first kiss, which closes volume 1. Fandom infobox 'Ch. 3-4'; Chapter 4 page reverse-maps to 'Ep. 3-4'.
Aftermath of the stolen kiss (ch 4) plus the front half of ch 5's park attack; ch 5's Pudding reveal is held back to ep 7. Fandom infobox 'Ch. 4-5'; Chapter 5 page reverse-maps to 'Ep. 4, ...'.

Bu-Ling/Pudding revealed as the fourth Mew - the back half of ch 5 per the volume-2 chapter-list summary ('The acrobatic girl is revealed to be Pudding Fong, the fourth Mew Mew'); Chapter 5's fandom page lists ep 4 plus unfilled further episodes. Re-uses ch 5, does not advance position past ep 4.

Zakuro identified as the fifth Mew, transforms unaided and coldly refuses to join. Volume 2 (ch 5-9) breaks into exactly five narrative beats in the Wikipedia chapter-list summary and this is beat 3; ja.wikipedia flags ep 10 as manga-based. Derived split, not a stated per-chapter source.
Studio battle with all five transformed, televised live, team introduces itself as 'Tokyo Mew Mew' - beat 4 of volume 2. ja.wikipedia flags ep 11 as manga-based.
Inohara Park chimera-anima fight ending with Masaya calling Mew Ichigo 'Ichigo' - the closing beat of volume 2 (beat 5). ja.wikipedia flags ep 12 as manga-based.

anchors.chapters_adapted: 10, plus the bell-ribbon beat grafted from ch 6
anchors.note: Ch 10 'Shall We Dance?': Ichigo avoids Masaya, Pie and Tart are sent in, and Masaya explains why he called her 'Ichigo'. The episode also lands ch 6's belled cat ribbon, which the manga placed back in volume 2. ja.wikipedia flags ep 13 as manga-based.

The Blue Knight's debut closes volume 4 in the manga (Ichigo alone against Quiche, rescued by a blond blue-eyed alien who swears to protect her). The anime pulls that beat forward here and rewrites the setup (Ichigo has a cold instead of being separated on a date). Chapters 11-15 are still unanimated at this point - see continue_points.

Volume 5 opens with the Blue Knight taking Quiche apart ('After they defeat the monster, the Blue Knight also easily defeats Quiche') and telling Ichigo he was born to protect her - ep 18's first act, with the anime softening it so he is injured. ja.wikipedia flags ep 18 as manga-based.

Closes volume 5 (Alto turns out to be Ryou) and opens volume 6 (Keiichiro tells the history of the Mew Project, Ryou having tested the merge on himself). Both beats are stated in the Wikipedia volume 5 and volume 6 summaries; ja.wikipedia flags ep 36 as manga-based. Ch 18 and 19 are still unanimated here - see continue_points.

Ch 22 'A Kiss for Kish': Quiche corners Ichigo, Masaya transforms into the Blue Knight for the first time on-screen and Quiche is left wondering what Masaya really is. ja.wikipedia flags ep 45 as manga-based.
Ch 24 'A Dome of Doom' ends volume 6 with the Blue Knight collapsing and transforming into Deep Blue - exactly ep 49's closing beat. ja.wikipedia flags ep 49 as manga-based.
Ch 25 'Deep Blue Revealed': Ichigo cannot bring herself to fight, Deep Blue flattens the other Mews and Alto/Ryou takes the blow meant for her. ja.wikipedia flags ep 50 as manga-based.

Ch 26 'You Love the Earth': Ichigo goes for the last mew aqua, Quiche duels Deep Blue and dies in her arms, and Masaya regains control of the body. The anime adds Pie's and Tart's deaths, which the manga does not have.

Series finale = the manga's final chapter. The ep 52 summary tracks the volume 7 summary almost beat for beat (mew aqua inside Masaya's body, both spirits pulled out, the city healed, aliens revived and sent home, Ichigo revived by Masaya's kiss). The anime replaces the manga's closing mock wedding with an a la Mode sequel hook. Repairs the stored mu anchor of 32 - see repairs.

continue_points.note: Ends inside ch 5 - only the front half of the park attack is animated; ch 5's Pudding reveal arrives at ep 7, so the honest resume is ch 5 itself (C1).

Ep 17 grafts ch 16's Blue Knight debut forward; chs 11-15 are still unanimated. Ch 11 (cruise ship) is never adapted, chs 12-15 arrive at eps 25-28. Reader resumes at 11 and will meet ch 16's debut again on arrival.
Same gap as ep 17 - after ch 17 the unread block is still chs 11-15; the anime returns to chs 14-15 at eps 25-26 and chs 12-13 at ep 28.

Ep 36 takes chs 20-21 out of order. Chs 18-19 are not yet animated at this point: ch 19 arrives at ep 38 and ch 18 at ep 40, so the reader who continues at 18 runs two episodes ahead of the anime on those two chapters.

annotations.note: Eps 1-13 adapt chs 1-10 in order, but eps 5-6, 8-9 are wholly anime-original padding inserted between them (AFL types them filler and the fandom episode infoboxes record no manga counterpart).
The belled cat ribbon / 'all-time favourite kitty' beat from ch 6 is relocated from volume 2 to the closing scene of ep 13.

The anime front-loads ch 16's Blue Knight debut (ep 17) and ch 17's duel (ep 18), then goes back: eps 25-26 adapt the Tokyo Tower cocoon/waiburn arc (chs 14-15, with the cocoon planting borrowed from ch 13), ep 27 adapts ch 16's rain confession, and ep 28 adapts chs 12-13 (Ichigo trapped in cat form, taken in by Masaya, Alto's first appearance). These four episodes are recorded here rather than as anchors because their END chapters run BEHIND ep 18's ch 17 and would make the anchor series non-monotonic.

Volume 4's internal ch 14 / 15 / 16 split could not be pinned to a source: en.wikipedia and the fandom volume page both summarise volume 4 as a whole (four narrative beats across three chapters) and no per-chapter page exists past ch 7. Zone-level only: eps 25-27 sit inside chs 14-16.

Mew Lettuce's legs turning into a porpoise fin is a manga beat from ch 21 (the red-tide rescue). The anime previews it here in a wholly original beach story, then plays the actual ch 21 version at ep 41.
Re-uses the mew-aqua briefing already animated with chs 8-9; Mint quitting the team and the fake mew aqua are anime-original. No new chapter coverage.

Ep 37 is an original Christmas set-up; ep 38 lands ch 19's payload - Ichigo tells Masaya she is a Mew Mew and he answers that he already knew and only pretended otherwise. Recorded as an annotation rather than an anchor because ch 19 sits behind ep 36's ch 21 (backfill), and because ja.wikipedia does not flag either episode as manga-based.

Ch 18 'Rescue Mission' - Pudding trapped under the Tokyo Dome with Tart, the candy, 'Taru-taru', and the trees grown to hold the dome up. Backfill behind ep 36's ch 21, hence an annotation rather than an anchor.

The red-tide / Tokyo Bay pollution half of ch 21, with Lettuce's porpoise fin activating to save Ryou. Ch 21 was already reached at ep 36, so this adds no position. ja.wikipedia does not flag ep 41 as manga-based even though our row types it canon.

Tokyo overgrown into a forest echoes ch 18's mew-aqua-grown trees, but the plot (mew aqua possibly made by the aliens, Ryou ruled out as the Blue Knight) is anime-original. ja.wikipedia does not flag ep 44 as manga-based.

Masaya formally joining the Mew Project, the river hunt and the octopus chimera anima have no manga counterpart; the manga never puts the Blue Knight on the team. Masaya's prophetic dream of Ichigo crying foreshadows ch 26. ja.wikipedia does not flag either episode as manga-based.

Carries ch 23's one load-bearing beat - Quiche telling Pie and Tart that the Blue Knight is the one who can save them (the manga has the three aliens bow before him). Ch 23's heat dome and Quiche's love confession/rejection are redistributed: the rejection plays at ep 45. Ch 23 is therefore only partly adapted and gets no anchor.
Ep 52 adapts ch 27 but swaps the manga's closing mock wedding and Masaya's study-abroad departure for a hook into Tokyo Mew Mew a la Mode.

Ch 11 (TokyoPop 'Cruise Control' - Pie attacking a cruise ship) has no counterpart anywhere in the 52-episode run; no episode summary on en.wikipedia or the fandom wiki contains a ship attack. Treat it as permanently skipped.

repairs.why: Chapter-space error, not a content error. The stored anchor is in a 32/33-chapter space (AniList reports 33 chapters, MangaDex metadata reports lastChapter 32) that counts the volumes' bonus material - Tokyo Black Cat Girl, Petite Mew Mew, the Bonus Comic, Sleeping Beauty of Berry Forest - as numbered chapters. The mainline chapter-NUMBER space used by the fandom wiki, the en.wikipedia chapter list AND by this series' stored volume boundaries (v1 1-4, v2 5-9, v3 10-13, v4 14-16, v5 17-20, v6 21-24, v7 25-...) runs 1-27, and the final chapter is ch 27 'A Transfer of Power', which is exactly what ep 52 adapts. Apply-script contract: this row's source is 'mu' (derivation tier), so the repair must flip the row to source 'manual' or the next mu re-derive will erase it.

structure.notes: One component, one season, 52 broadcast episodes (2002-04-06 to 2003-03-29, TV Aichi / TXN); our cumulative numbering equals broadcast numbering 1:1, no OVAs, no movies, no specials. NUMBERING TRAP: the 4Kids dub 'Mew Mew Power' reorders and renumbers the first 26 episodes (its ep 1 is Japanese ep 12, its ep 3 is Japanese ep 2, etc.) and tokyomewmew.fandom.com hosts a parallel set of 'Episode NN: <dub title>' pages using that numbering - every number in this verdict is Japanese broadcast numbering, taken from pages titled with the Japanese episode title, never from the 'Episode NN:' dub pages. WIKI LIMITATION: the fandom episode infobox has a 'chapter' field but it is only filled for eps 1-4 (eps 5-6 are explicitly '<!-- none -->'); every episode page from ep 7 on carries a literal '...' placeholder, and episodes 27+ are stubs with no infobox chapter field at all. Chapter pages exist only for chs 1-7, and only chs 1-5 carry a reverse 'anime' mapping. Everything past ep 4 in this verdict is therefore beat-alignment between the en.wikipedia chapter-list volume summaries and the en.wikipedia / fandom episode summaries, cross-checked against ja.wikipedia's bolded 'episodes based on the original work' flags - stated honestly as medium. MANGA STRUCTURE: 7 volumes; chapter-number space 1-27 (v1 1-4, v2 5-9, v3 10-13, v4 14-16, v5 17-20, v6 21-24, v7 25-27), matching the stored volume boundaries. ADAPTATION SHAPE: linear for eps 1-13 (chs 1-10) and eps 49-52 (chs 24-27); non-linear in between, with forward grafts at eps 17-18 and backfill at eps 25-28, 38, 40. 21 of 52 episodes are typed filler in our rows and AFL puts the series at ~40% filler.

flags_for_sean: CHAPTER SPACE: four sources give four different totals for this manga - en.wikipedia + fandom chapter LISTS = 27 numbered chapters (this is the space our stored volume boundaries use, and the space every anchor above is in); en.wikipedia article PROSE says 'the twenty-nine chapters', and the fandom trivia repeats that TokyoPop 'mistakenly put down 27'; MangaDex metadata says lastChapter 32; AniList (our entry, total_chapters) says 33. If the entry stays at 33, ep 52 -> ch 27 renders as ~82% of the manga rather than the end of it. Recommend total_chapters 27, or an explicit conversion note.

NON-MONOTONIC ADAPTATION: eps 25-28 (chs 12-16), 38 (ch 19) and 40 (ch 18) genuinely adapt chapters BEHIND the furthest point already reached at eps 18 and 36. I recorded them as annotations rather than anchors so the anchor series stays monotonic. If the pipeline tolerates backward END values these six are ready to promote to anchors: 25->14, 26->15, 27->16, 28->13 (start 12), 38->19, 40->18.

TYPE DISAGREEMENT (not corrected - only one source dissents each way): ja.wikipedia bolds eps 5 and 6 as 'based on the original work' while AFL types them filler and the fandom infoboxes explicitly say no manga counterpart (left as filler). Conversely ja.wikipedia does NOT bold eps 37, 38, 41, 44, 47, 48 although our rows type them canon/mixed; content checks show 38, 41 and 48 do carry real manga beats (chs 19, 21, 23) while 44, 46 and 47 look anime-original. Worth a second pass if type accuracy matters here.

VOLUME 4 INTERNAL SPLIT UNRESOLVED: no source states where ch 14 ends and chs 15/16 begin - en.wikipedia and the fandom volume page both summarise volume 4 as one block containing four beats across three chapters, and no chapter page exists past ch 7. Eps 25/26/27 are therefore zone-level (chs 14-16) rather than chapter-exact, and ep 17's END of 16 rests on the Blue Knight debut being the volume's closing beat.

CH 11 NEVER ADAPTED: TokyoPop 'Cruise Control' (Pie attacks a cruise ship) has no counterpart in any of the 52 episode summaries. Any continue point that steps over it should say so rather than let a reader think they missed an episode.
